g202.text: A supermarket trolley! Which material would you choose to make it? One, glass. Two, metal. Three, fabric.

g301.text: You against the Buddies! Lock in first. One finger for every point. A little mynah is hiding in this video. Can you spot it?

h501.text: Are you ready? Three! Two! One! Go!

g501.text: First: what is a trolley for? Look closer.

g502.text: A bag of rice goes in. Bottles. Tins. It is heavy now.

g503.text: A push, and it all rolls along.

g504.text: A trolley is for carrying heavy groceries. That is its purpose.

g602.text: Materials are used to make objects. Objects are things you use for different purposes.

g603.text: A towel. Scissors. A raincoat. Each has its own purpose.

g701.text: Round one: the question from last time! Glass, metal, or fabric? Show me your fingers!

g703.text: One! Glass! I can see all my snacks!

g704.text: Three. My fabric bag carries heavy books, and it does not tear.

g705.text: Two! The trolleys here are all metal!

g801.text: Look closer. The metal trolley, full of heavy groceries.

g802.text: The metal bars stay straight. They do not bend.

g803.text: Now it rolls into the trolley bay. Clang! A hard knock.

g804.text: No crack. No break. Metal is strong.

g805.text: Glass is fragile, but metal is strong. A glass cup breaks easily when it is dropped, but a metal cup does not.

g807.text: And fabric? Pip's bag holds the rice. But it folds flat: fabric is flexible.

g808.text: Oh! A trolley must not bend!

g809.text: The answer is two. Metal! Two fingers? One finger up!

g902.text: Every material has physical properties. The physical properties of a material allow it to be used in certain ways.

g1001.text: So glass is a bad material! Never use glass for anything!

g1002.text: Something is not right. If you can spot it, cross your arms. Hold on!

g1003.text: Arms crossed? One finger up! Glass is not a bad material. It depends on the use.

g1004.text: Hold on, Momo! The fish tank next door is glass!

g1101.text: Look closer. A glass fish tank, full of water.

g1102.text: We can see every fish clearly. Glass is transparent.

g1103.text: The shelf under it is dry. No water passes through. Glass is waterproof.

g1104.text: For a fish tank, glass is the right material!

g1105.text: Oh! The same glass. A different use!

g1201.text: Be the metal! Shrink down. Quietly.

g1202.text: You are a metal bar, at the bottom of the trolley.

g1203.text: A heavy bag of rice lands on you. You do not bend.

g1204.text: The wheels roll. The floor rushes past.

g1205.text: Clang! A hard knock. You do not break. You are strong!

g1301.text: Show me your score hand! One finger or more? You beat the Buddies. Two fingers? High five!

g1302.text: Did you spot the mynah? It was on the trolley bay sign!

g1302f.text: Here's a fun fact! Mynahs build their nests from dry grass, twigs, string, and even bits of plastic!

h860.text: Let's read today's key words together! Ready?

g1401.text: Look! Three water bottles in our trolley!

g1402.text: One plastic. One glass. One metal. The same object, three materials! Which one is right for school?
